subject.title: [Feature Request]: Native Prompt Caching Support for Amazon Nova (Bedrock)

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally change direct Amazon Bedrock Nova from forced no-cache to native cache-point eligible behavior once live Nova proof is attached?
rationale: Source proves the requested behavior is missing, but enabling Nova prompt caching changes provider request shaping and default behavior for existing Nova users, and the active PR still lacks live provider proof.

options.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
options.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

options.title: Require opt-in Nova caching
options.body: Preserve no-cache as the upgrade default and allow Nova cache points only through explicit configuration or a narrower policy gate.

options.title: Defer Nova native caching
options.body: Leave the current no-cache behavior in place until AWS docs, live proof, or provider ownership makes the default behavior less uncertain.

recommendation.title: Land the linked provider fix after live proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted Nova Converse or ConverseStream proof, then accept the provider-owned policy change in the linked PR or a narrow replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Bedrock provider and current-main line history make this the strongest available routing signal for the provider behavior decision.
